answer: The Adele E. Clarke Book Award from ReproNetwork

question: A quantum optics technique leveraging second-order nonlinearity for generating correlated photon pairs was first experimentally observed in the same decade that continuous-wave dye lasers became practical. Among the early researchers was a Stanford professor who began his tenure there in a year that matches the difference between when a certain physicist—known for contributions to both dislocation theory and high-temperature creep phenomena, and who received a military honor for wartime service—published his seminal monograph and when that Stanford professor started at Stanford. This physicist once headed the physics department at a South African university where, in the same year that a major national photonics conference was held, a laboratory focusing on spatial light manipulation was established. The director of this laboratory serves on the editorial board of a journal that in April 2026 published a breakthrough achieving a megawatt-class optical vortex array. What is the sum of the peak power (in megawatts) of this optical vortex array and the number of years between the publication of the dislocation theorist's seminal book and the year the Stanford professor began his tenure?
